title: en agapē: "holy in love" or "predestined in love"?
summary: Greek has no punctuation, so the phrase "in love" can close v. 4 (holy and blameless before him in love) or open v. 5 (in love he predestined us). Translations and the Vulgate divide on where the sentence break falls.

readings.label: With "holy and blameless before him"
readings.rendering: that we should be holy and blameless before him in love. He predestined us...
readings.grammar: ἐν ἀγάπῃ closes the εἶναι ἡμᾶς ἁγίους καὶ ἀμώμους κατενώπιον αὐτοῦ clause; προορίσας then begins the next phrase. "Love" is then the believers' love (or the sphere of their holiness).

fathers.quote: These are the ones whom he elected before the world in Christ, so that they might be blameless before God through love

readings.label: With "predestined us"
readings.rendering: In love he predestined us to adoption as sons...
readings.grammar: ἐν ἀγάπῃ is placed before the participle προορίσας: God's love is the manner or motive of predestination.

fathers.quote: In love, says he, having predestinated us. Because this comes not of any pains, nor of any good works of ours, but of love;

macula_evidence: The tree places ἐν ἀγάπῃ inside the εἶναι... κατενώπιον αὐτοῦ phrase, with προορίσας ἡμᾶς as a separate adverbial clause: it encodes the "holy in love" attachment.

title: "His inheritance in the saints": whose inheritance?
summary: The genitive "his inheritance" with "in the saints" can describe the inheritance God possesses in his people (subjective) or the inheritance he gives, whose riches are found among the saints (the believers' future share).

readings.label: God's inheritance in the saints
readings.rendering: the riches of the glory of God's own inheritance, which is the saints
readings.grammar: αὐτοῦ is a possessive/subjective genitive: God is the heir; ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις locates his possession among the holy ones (cf. Deut 32:9).
readings.modern: Held by many modern commentators (e.g. Lincoln, Best)

readings.label: The inheritance God gives to the saints
readings.rendering: the riches of the glory of the inheritance he gives, in the saints
readings.grammar: αὐτοῦ is a genitive of source: the inheritance comes from God and is the believers' hope; ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις is read as "among/for the saints".

fathers.quote: He likewise will grant "the enlightenment of the eyes of the understanding". In His gift, too, are "the riches (of the glory) of His inheritance in the saints"

macula_evidence: The tree attaches αὐτοῦ to κληρονομίας and ἐν τοῖς ἁγίοις to the same noun phrase but does not say whose inheritance or whether ἐν is locative.

title: plērōma and plēroumenou: who fills whom?
summary: πληρουμένου can be passive (Christ is being filled) or middle (Christ fills for himself everything everywhere); πλήρωμα itself can mean "that which fills up/completes" or "that which is filled". The church is "the fullness" of Christ in one of these senses.

readings.label: Passive: the church completes Christ
readings.rendering: the fullness of him who is filled all in all
readings.grammar: πληρουμένου passive; πλήρωμα in the sense of "complement": Christ the head is filled up by his body.

fathers.quote: It is by all then that His body is filled up. Then is the head filled up, then is the body rendered perfect, when we are all knit together and united.

readings.label: Middle: Christ fills everything
readings.rendering: the fullness of him who fills all in all
readings.grammar: πληρουμένου middle voice with active force (as in Eph 4:10, "fills all things"); the church is the sphere in which Christ's fullness is present.

fathers.quote: Having recovered all things again through the mystery of salvation and saved the full number of souls, Christ is filling all in all.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses πληρουμένου as "fills" (middle/active sense) in a relative clause modifying the Christ-referent.

title: "The ruler of the power of the air, of the spirit": what is "the spirit"?
summary: τοῦ πνεύματος is genitive after "ruler" or after "authority"/"air". It can be in apposition to the ruler (the devil is the spirit), or name the spirit-force (disposition, realm) over which he has authority.

readings.label: Apposition: the ruler is the spirit
readings.rendering: the ruler... the spirit now at work in the sons of disobedience
readings.grammar: τοῦ πνεύματος loosely in apposition to τὸν ἄρχοντα (case attraction): the devil himself is the spirit at work.

fathers.quote: He is therefore that spirit now at work through material means among the children of disobedience.

readings.label: A spirit-force under his authority
readings.rendering: the ruler of the realm of the air, of the spirit (force) now at work
readings.grammar: τοῦ πνεύματος dependent on ἐξουσίας: the realm of authority is the spirit-world or the pervading disposition of the age.

fathers.quote: Here again he means, that Satan occupies the space under Heaven, and that the incorporeal powers are spirits of the air, under his operation.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses "ruler the power the air the spirit" in one chain and hangs the "now at work" relative clause on πνεύματος; it does not state whether the last genitive is apposition or dependent.

title: touto: what is "not of yourselves"?
summary: "This" (neuter τοῦτο) cannot agree grammatically with feminine πίστις, so it may point back to the whole statement ("you are saved by grace through faith") or loosely to faith itself. The question is what is the "gift of God".

readings.label: Faith is the gift
readings.rendering: and this faith is not from yourselves; it is God's gift
readings.grammar: τοῦτο refers to πίστεως by sense (a neuter demonstrative may refer to a feminine antecedent in sense).

fathers.quote: Neither is faith, he means, of ourselves. Because had He not come, had He not called us, how had we been able to believe? For how, says he, shall they believe, unless they hear? So that the work of faith itself is not our own.

readings.label: The whole salvation is the gift
readings.rendering: and this salvation (by grace through faith) is not from yourselves
readings.grammar: neuter τοῦτο has as antecedent the entire clause σεσῳσμένοι διὰ πίστεως; no gender mismatch.
readings.modern: Most modern grammarians and commentators (Wallace, Hoehner, NET)

macula_evidence: The tree makes καὶ τοῦτο οὐκ ἐξ ὑμῶν a separate clause with τοῦτο as subject; it does not identify the antecedent.

title: "The foundation of the apostles and prophets": what kind of genitive?
summary: The genitive "of the apostles and prophets" can say the apostles and prophets are themselves the foundation (apposition), or that the foundation is what they laid or taught (source/agent), with Christ then the cornerstone.

readings.label: Apposition: the apostles and prophets are the foundation
readings.rendering: built on the foundation which is the apostles and prophets
readings.grammar: τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ προφητῶν is a genitive of apposition/epexegesis: the persons are the foundation, with Christ as ἀκρογωνιαῖος.

fathers.quote: that is, the Apostles and Prophets are a foundation, and he places the Apostles first, though they are in order of time last, doubtless to represent and express this, that both the one and the other are alike a foundation, and that the whole is one building, and that there is one root.

readings.label: Source: the foundation they laid (their teaching)
readings.rendering: built on the foundation laid by the apostles and prophets, namely Christ and their witness
readings.grammar: τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ προφητῶν is a genitive of source/agency: the teaching or witness the apostles and prophets gave, resting on Christ.

fathers.quote: This foundation is the teaching of the apostles, which is also heard in the word of the prophets.

macula_evidence: The tree attaches the genitive to θεμελίῳ and does not classify it; ὄντος ἀκρογωνιαίου αὐτοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ is a separate adverbial phrase.

title: pasa oikodomē: "every building" or "the whole building"?
summary: Anarthrous πᾶσα with a singular noun normally means "every", but with some nouns (and in Koine) "whole". Here it decides whether each local community is a growing temple or the whole church is one.

readings.label: "Every building" (each part or local church)
readings.rendering: in whom every building, being fitted together, grows into a holy temple
readings.grammar: πᾶσα without the article distributes: each structure or stage of construction.

readings.label: "The whole building"
readings.rendering: in whom the whole building, being fitted together, grows into a holy temple
readings.grammar: πᾶσα with a singular noun can mean "the whole, all" in later Greek; the unit is the single household/temple of v. 19-22.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses πᾶσα οἰκοδομή as "whole building".

title: dia tēs pisteōs autou: faith in him or his faithfulness?
summary: The genitive "his faith" can be objective (faith directed to Christ) or subjective (Christ's own faithfulness), the same question that surrounds pistis Christou in Romans and Galatians.

readings.label: Objective genitive: faith in him
readings.rendering: access with confidence through faith in him
readings.grammar: αὐτοῦ is an objective genitive: πίστις is the believer's trust in Christ.

fathers.quote: we have even boldness with confidence, that is, accompanied with cheerful trust; arising from what source? through our faith in Him.

readings.label: Subjective genitive: his faithfulness
readings.rendering: access with confidence through his (Christ's) faithfulness
readings.grammar: αὐτοῦ is a subjective genitive: the faithfulness Christ himself showed gives access.
readings.modern: Proponents of the "faithfulness of Christ" reading of pistis Christou (e.g. Hays; NET alternative)

macula_evidence: The tree glosses the phrase "faith his" without classifying the genitive.

title: "The lower parts of the earth": apposition or partitive?
summary: τῆς γῆς can be a genitive of apposition ("the lower parts, namely the earth"), or partitive ("the lower regions within/of the earth", Hades), or comparative ("lower than the earth"). The choice decides whether the verse speaks of the incarnation or a descent to the dead.

readings.label: Apposition: the earth itself
readings.rendering: he descended into the lower regions, that is, the earth (incarnation, death)
readings.grammar: τῆς γῆς in apposition to τὰ κατώτερα μέρη: the descent is from heaven to earth.
readings.modern: Held by many Protestant and some Catholic commentators

fathers.quote: When you hear these words, think not of a mere removal from one place to another; for what Paul establishes in the Epistle to the Philippians Philippians 2:5-8, that very argument is he also insisting upon here. In the same way as there, when exhorting them concerning lowliness, he brings forward Christ as an example, so does he here also, saying, He descended into the lower parts of the earth. For were not this so, this expression which he uses, He became obedient even unto death Philippians 2:8-9, were superfluous; whereas from His ascending, he implies His descent, and by the lower parts of the earth, he means death

readings.label: Partitive: the underworld within the earth
readings.rendering: he descended into the lower parts of the earth (Hades)
readings.grammar: τῆς γῆς partitive: the lower regions belonging to the earth, i.e. the realm of the dead.

traditions.catholic: Often cited with 1 Pet 3:19 for the descent into Hades in the Creed

fathers.quote: Therefore, after his triumph over the devil, he descended to the heart of the world, so that he might preach to the dead, that all who desired him might be set free.

macula_evidence: The tree reads εἰς τὰ κατώτερα μέρη τῆς γῆς as one prepositional phrase and gives no classification of the genitive.

title: Eph 4:12: three parallel goals, or saints equipped for ministry?
summary: The three prepositional phrases (πρὸς... εἰς... εἰς...) can be coordinate purposes of the gifted offices, or the first is the main goal with the next two subordinate (equip the saints so that they do the ministry).

readings.label: Three coordinate goals of the offices
readings.rendering: to perfect the saints, to do the work of ministry, to build up the body
readings.grammar: Comma after ἁγίων; πρὸς, εἰς, εἰς are parallel: the apostles, prophets and pastors perfect, minister and edify.

fathers.quote: For the perfecting of the saints unto the work of ministering, unto the building up of the body of Christ. Perceive ye the dignity of the office? Each one edifies, each one perfects, each one ministers.

readings.label: Equipping the saints for ministry
readings.rendering: to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up the body
readings.grammar: No comma after ἁγίων: εἰς ἔργον διακονίας is subordinate to πρὸς τὸν καταρτισμὸν τῶν ἁγίων; the saints are the ministers.

macula_evidence: The tree sets πρὸς τὸν καταρτισμόν, εἰς ἔργον and εἰς οἰκοδομήν as sister phrases under ἔδωκεν, encoding the coordinate (comma) reading.

title: Eph 5:21-22: does the household code borrow its verb from v. 21?
summary: Verse 22 has no verb. Either it borrows "submit" from the participle ὑποτασσόμενοι in v. 21, which then heads the household code (mutual submission), or v. 21 closes the Spirit-filled participle chain of vv. 18-21 and v. 22 supplies its own implied verb.

readings.label: v. 21 heads the household code (mutual submission)
readings.rendering: Submit to one another out of reverence for Christ. Wives, (submit) to your own husbands
readings.grammar: ὑποτασσόμενοι governs v. 22 by ellipsis; ἀλλήλοις makes submission mutual, the husband's role then defined by love.

fathers.quote: He says, submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of Christ. And what then if another submit not himself? Still obey thou the law of God.

readings.label: v. 21 ends the participle chain; v. 22 starts a new unit
readings.rendering: Be filled with the Spirit... submitting to one another. Wives, (be subject) to your own husbands
readings.grammar: ὑποτασσόμενοι is the last of the participles dependent on πληροῦσθε (v. 18); v. 22 implies a new imperative, so submission in vv. 22ff is asymmetrical.

macula_evidence: The tree attaches ὑποτασσόμενοι to the participle chain under πληροῦσθε ἐν πνεύματι and treats v. 22 as a separate verbless clause.

title: "The washing of water by the word": what is "the word"?
summary: ἐν ῥήματι can modify λουτρῷ (the washing with the spoken word, the baptismal formula) or καθαρίσας/ἁγιάσῃ (cleansing by the gospel word of faith); and ῥῆμα can mean the formula spoken over the water or the preached message.

readings.label: The baptismal formula
readings.rendering: cleansing her by the washing of water with the word (spoken in baptism)
readings.grammar: ἐν ῥήματι attaches to τῷ λουτρῷ τοῦ ὕδατος: the word is the invocation or confession pronounced at baptism.

traditions.catholic: Word as the baptismal form (Trinitarian invocation)

fathers.quote: By the washing or laver He washes her uncleanness. By the word, says he. What word? In the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.

fathers.work: Tractates on the Gospel of John
fathers.quote: Take away the water, it is no baptism; take away the Word, it is no baptism.

readings.label: The gospel word of faith
readings.rendering: cleansing her by the washing of water through the word (the gospel preached and believed)
readings.grammar: ἐν ῥήματι is instrumental with καθαρίσας: the spoken or preached message is the means of cleansing, with the water as accompaniment.

traditions.protestant: Often read as the gospel word received by faith

macula_evidence: The tree reads "cleansing the washing of the water by word" as a single phrase under καθαρίσας, without deciding the attachment of ἐν ῥήματι.

title: "This mystery is great": which mystery?
summary: τὸ μυστήριον τοῦτο can point back to the one-flesh union of Gen 2:24 in marriage (hence the Latin sacramentum), or to the union of Christ and the church as the real meaning of that text; εἰς Χριστόν can mean "in reference to" or "toward".

readings.label: The mystery is marriage (as a sign of Christ and the church)
readings.rendering: this sacrament (marriage) is great; I speak in reference to Christ and the church
readings.grammar: τοῦτο refers to the quoted one-flesh union (v. 31) as itself a mystery; εἰς Χριστόν indicates what it signifies.

traditions.catholic: Vulgate sacramentum; cited at Trent (Sess. 24) for the sacrament of matrimony
traditions.orthodox: Marriage as a mystery of the Church

fathers.quote: The apostle speaks of a great mystery in the relation of Christ and the church. That which is great in respect of Christ and the church may seem less auspicious in the relation between husbands and wives. But in marriage it still represents the mystery of an inseparable bond.

readings.label: The mystery is Christ and the church; marriage only a type
readings.rendering: this mystery is great, and I mean it of Christ and the church
readings.grammar: τοῦτο refers to the true sense of Gen 2:24, which concerns Christ and the church; ἐγὼ δὲ λέγω εἰς Χριστόν limits the meaning.

traditions.protestant: Reformers read it as typology of Christ and the church, not a sacrament

fathers.quote: For the present, however, says he, I speak regarding Christ, that having left the Father, He came down, and came to the Bride, and became one Spirit. For he that is joined unto the Lord is one Spirit. And well says he, it is a great mystery.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses εἰς Χριστὸν καὶ εἰς τὴν ἐκκλησίαν as "as to Christ and the church" but does not say what τοῦτο points back to.

title: Phil 2:5: "which was also in Christ Jesus" or "which is yours in Christ Jesus"?
summary: The clause "which also in Christ Jesus" has no verb. Supplying "was" makes Christ's mindset the example to imitate; supplying "is" (or "you have") makes "in Christ Jesus" the believers' sphere of life, with the hymn that follows as grounding rather than model.

readings.label: Christ is the example (supply "was")
readings.rendering: Have this mind among you which was also in Christ Jesus
readings.grammar: ὃ καὶ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ with ἦν understood: the pre-existent and incarnate Christ's attitude is the pattern.

fathers.quote: Our Lord Jesus Christ, when exhorting His disciples to great actions, places before them Himself, and the Father, and the Prophets, as examples;
For the first, his humility, is manifest, since Christ humbled himself and assumed the character of a slave.

readings.label: "In Christ" is the believers' sphere (supply "is yours")
readings.rendering: Have this mind among you, which is yours in Christ Jesus
readings.grammar: ἐν ὑμῖν = "among you" and ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ = "in the community of Christ"; the verb supplied is ἐστιν/ὑμῖν.

macula_evidence: The tree gives ὃ καὶ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ as a separate verbless clause; it does not supply a verb or decide between "was" and "is".

title: harpagmon: "a thing to be grasped," "to be held onto," or "robbery"?
summary: ἁρπαγμός is rare. With οὐχ ... ἡγήσατο it can mean (a) something not yet possessed to be seized, (b) something already possessed that is not to be clung to or exploited, or (c) in the Latin tradition, that equality was no usurpation because it was his by nature.

readings.label: Res rapienda: not grasping at equality he lacked
readings.rendering: did not consider equality with God something to be seized
readings.grammar: ἁρπαγμός = res rapienda (an object of seizure); τὸ εἶναι ἴσα θεῷ is the thing sought; ὑπάρχων is concessive-contrastive with the Adam parallel.
readings.modern: Held by Adam-parallel readers and some Greek-speaking opponents of Nicene equality (noted and refuted by Chrysostom)

readings.label: Res retinenda: equality possessed but not clung to
readings.rendering: did not consider equality with God something to be exploited or clung to
readings.grammar: ἁρπαγμός = res retinenda / "an advantage to be used"; οὐχ ... ἀλλά contrasts equality retained with self-emptying; ὑπάρχων is concessive.
readings.modern: Most modern scholars after Hoover (1971): NRSV, ESV, NIV, NAB

fathers.quote: Whatsoever a man robs, and takes contrary to his right, he dares not lay aside, from fear lest it perish, and fall from his possession, but he keeps hold of it continually.

readings.label: "Not robbery": equality was his by nature
readings.rendering: did not think it robbery to be equal with God
readings.grammar: ἁρπαγμός understood as "a seizure/usurpation"; οὐχ ἁρπαγμὸν ἡγήσατο = he did not consider equality a usurpation (Latin non rapinam arbitratus).
readings.modern: KJV, Vulgate, Douay: "thought it not robbery"

fathers.quote: He did not rob, because who he was, he was by nature.
It would be a kind of robbery if two things were not equal by nature but were forced to be made equal or made equal through some accident.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses οὐχ ἁρπαγμὸν ἡγήσατο as "not something to be exploited" with τὸ εἶναι ἴσα θεῷ as object, matching the res retinenda reading.

title: dia pisteōs Christou: faith in Christ or Christ's faithfulness?
summary: The genitive Χριστοῦ after πίστεως can be objective (faith placed in Christ) or subjective (the faithfulness of Christ), parallel to Rom 3:22 and Gal 2:16. The following phrase "on the basis of faith" (ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει) is taken as support for either.

readings.label: Objective genitive: faith in Christ
readings.rendering: through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God that depends on faith
readings.grammar: Χριστοῦ is an objective genitive; πίστις is the believer's trust, and ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει repeats it.
readings.modern: Traditional view: KJV "faith of Christ" read objectively; NIV, ESV, NASB

readings.label: Subjective genitive: the faithfulness of Christ
readings.rendering: through the faithfulness of Christ, the righteousness from God that depends on faith
readings.grammar: Χριστοῦ is a subjective genitive; Christ's obedient faithfulness grounds justification, and ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει then gives the believer's response.
readings.modern: NET text, NRSV margin; Hays, Wright, Campbell

macula_evidence: The tree attaches Χριστοῦ to πίστεως and gives no case classification.

title: "Firstborn of all creation": what kind of genitive?
summary: πάσης κτίσεως after πρωτότοκος can be partitive (Christ is the first of the created order), comparative (born before all creation), or a genitive of rank (heir and sovereign over creation). The choice bears on the Arian controversy.

readings.label: Partitive: first among creatures (new creation)
readings.rendering: the firstborn within creation
readings.grammar: πάσης κτίσεως is a partitive genitive: Christ belongs to the set "creation" (used by Arians; the Fathers who took it so limited it to the new creation).

fathers.quote: we recognize a twofold creation of our nature, the first that of our conception and birth, the second that of our new creation.

readings.label: Comparative: born before all creation
readings.rendering: begotten before all creation
readings.grammar: πάσης κτίσεως is a genitive of comparison (πρῶτος in a comparative sense = prior to); the next verse says all things were created in him, so he cannot be one of them.
readings.modern: Many Nicene-tradition commentators; NIV "over all creation" with note

fathers.quote: demonstrates that the Son of God is other than the whole creation and not a creature
For the word firstborn is not expressive of dignity and honor, nor of anything else, but of time only
Firstborn, mark you, not first created, in order that he may be believed to be both begotten, in virtue of his nature, and the first in virtue of his eternity.

readings.label: Rank: heir and ruler over creation
readings.rendering: the firstborn, the heir and sovereign over all creation
readings.grammar: πρωτότοκος as a title of rank (Ps 89:27); the genitive is a genitive of subordination: the firstborn has priority over, not temporal precedence before.
readings.modern: Common among modern commentators (cf. Exod 4:22, Ps 89:27)

macula_evidence: The tree attaches πάσης κτίσεως to πρωτότοκος as a genitive; the semantic class is not marked.

title: en autō ektisthē ta panta: "in him" as sphere, ground or agent?
summary: ἐν αὐτῷ with the passive ἐκτίσθη can express agency ("by him"), sphere or ground ("within the scope of his person"), or the place of the creative plan. The following δι᾽ αὐτοῦ keeps the instrument distinct.

readings.label: Instrumental or agent: created by him
readings.rendering: in (by) him all things were created
readings.grammar: ἐν = ἐν instrumental/agent, parallel to δι᾽ αὐτοῦ; Christ is the creator.

fathers.quote: has also plainly said that all things were made in the Son

readings.label: Locative or ground: in him as the sphere or source of creative power
readings.rendering: in him (as the sphere of the creative wisdom) all things were created
readings.grammar: ἐν locative/causal; ἐν αὐτῷ names the ground within which creation happens, distinct from δι᾽ αὐτοῦ (agent) and εἰς αὐτόν (goal).

fathers.quote: He is saying that the potency of all things may be believed to be in him

macula_evidence: The tree glosses ἐν αὐτῷ ἐκτίσθη as "in him ... created" with no choice between agency and sphere.

title: Col 1:19: who "was pleased" for the fullness to dwell?
summary: εὐδόκησεν has no stated subject. Either πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα is the subject of both εὐδόκησεν and κατοικῆσαι ("all the fullness was pleased to dwell"), or God is the implied subject ("[God] was pleased that all the fullness should dwell").

readings.label: The fullness is the subject
readings.rendering: all the fullness (of God) was pleased to dwell in him
readings.grammar: πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα is subject of εὐδόκησεν and the infinitive κατοικῆσαι (the fullness is personified).

readings.label: God is the implied subject
readings.rendering: (God) was pleased for all the fullness to dwell in him
readings.grammar: The subject of εὐδόκησεν is understood from context (God); πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα is the subject of the infinitive.

macula_evidence: The tree treats εὐδόκησεν as a verb with no subject of its own and makes the clause ἐν αὐτῷ πᾶν τὸ πλήρωμα κατοικῆσαι its object.

title: "What is lacking in Christ's afflictions": whose afflictions, and lacking how?
summary: τῶν θλίψεων τοῦ Χριστοῦ can be a genitive of possession (Christ himself suffers in his body the church), of cause or association (sufferings borne for Christ's cause), or of the Messiah's allotted woes. This determines in what sense something is "lacking" (ὑστερήματα).

readings.label: Possession: Christ suffers in his body
readings.rendering: what is lacking in the afflictions that Christ endures in his body, the church
readings.grammar: τοῦ Χριστοῦ is a genitive of possession/identification (head and body are one Christ); ὑστέρημα is the body's share still to be borne.

fathers.quote: thus showing that what he was suffering was part and parcel of the afflictions of Christ.
it is he himself who suffers.

readings.label: Cause or association: sufferings for Christ's cause
readings.rendering: what is lacking in the afflictions that come on account of Christ and his gospel
readings.grammar: τοῦ Χριστοῦ is a genitive of cause/association: sufferings arising from preaching Christ, like his.

fathers.work: Pauline Commentary from the Greek Church
fathers.quote: Because in order to preach to you, I have had to suffer.

readings.label: The Messiah's appointed quota of woes
readings.rendering: what remains of the messianic afflictions appointed before the end
readings.grammar: θλίψεις τοῦ Χριστοῦ as the eschatological "birth pangs" belonging to the Messiah's people; ὑστερήματα is a quantity that must be completed.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses ἀνταναπληρῶ τὰ ὑστερήματα τῶν θλίψεων τοῦ Χριστοῦ as "fill up what ... Christ's" and takes ἐν τῇ σαρκί μου with the verb; the genitive is not classified.

title: "Christ in you": within each person or among you Gentiles?
summary: ἐν ὑμῖν can be "in you" (indwelling) or "among you" (presence in the community), and since the relative ὅ refers to the mystery "among the Gentiles", the two prepositions may be parallel or contrasting.

readings.label: "In you": the indwelling Christ
readings.rendering: the mystery, which is Christ in you, the hope of glory
readings.grammar: ἐν ὑμῖν individual or corporate locative = "within you"; ὅ = the mystery, Christ himself.

readings.label: "Among you": Christ present among the Gentiles
readings.rendering: the mystery, which is Christ among you, the hope of glory
readings.grammar: ἐν ὑμῖν parallel to ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν (v. 27a): Christ present among the Gentile community.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses ἐν ὑμῖν as "in you" but does not choose between locative "within" and "among".

title: apekdusamenos: stripping off whom? and who is the subject?
summary: ἀπεκδυσάμενος is a middle participle of a compound "strip off". It can be reflexive (Christ stripped off from himself the powers/flesh) or have an active sense (stripped the powers of their authority, disarmed them), and the subject can be Christ or God.

readings.label: Middle: Christ put off from himself the powers (or the flesh)
readings.rendering: having put off from himself the principalities and powers
readings.grammar: ἀπεκδυσάμενος genuinely middle: reflexive "strip off from oneself"; the powers (or the flesh) were as a garment.

fathers.quote: When he became man he put away from himself that hold.

fathers.work: Pauline Commentary from the Greek Church
fathers.quote: Through the exposing and putting off of the flesh Christ subdued the opposing powers

readings.label: Active sense: stripped/disarmed the powers
readings.rendering: disarming the principalities and powers
readings.grammar: ἀπεκδυσάμενος with transitive force: the powers are stripped of their weapons and authority (a middle with active sense, as in 2:11).

macula_evidence: The tree glosses ἀπεκδυσάμενος τὰς ἀρχὰς καὶ τὰς ἐξουσίας as "disarmed the rulers and the authorities".

title: Col 2:15: "triumphing over them in it/him": the cross or Christ?
summary: αὐτῷ at the end of the verse can be masculine (Christ, the nearest personal subject) or neuter (the cross of v. 14), changing where the triumph takes place.

readings.label: "In it": the cross
readings.rendering: triumphing over them in (by) the cross
readings.grammar: αὐτῷ neuter, referring to τῷ σταυρῷ in v. 14.

readings.label: "In him": Christ
readings.rendering: triumphing over them in him (Christ)
readings.grammar: αὐτῷ masculine, referring to Christ, the subject of the whole sentence.

fathers.quote: and therefore he openly exposed the principalities and the powers, confidently triumphing over them in himself.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses αὐτῷ as "in it", taking the cross as antecedent.

title: threskeia tōn angelōn: worship of angels, or worship by angels?
summary: The genitive can be objective (worship directed to angels) or subjective (the worship the angels offer, which the opponents claim to share through visions). The word θρησκεία itself is not in dispute.

readings.label: Objective genitive: worship of angels
readings.rendering: delighting in humility and the worship of angels
readings.grammar: τῶν ἀγγέλων objective: the opponents offered cult to angels as mediators.

fathers.quote: There are some who maintain that we must be brought near by angels, not by Christ; for Christ to do so would seem too great an act on our behalf.

fathers.work: Pauline Commentary from the Greek Church
fathers.quote: Since, then, we cannot get near him, it is through his angels that propitiation comes and we may draw near him.

readings.label: Subjective genitive: the worship angels offer
readings.rendering: delighting in humility and the angelic worship (which he claims to join)
readings.grammar: τῶν ἀγγέλων subjective: the opponents claimed visionary participation in the heavenly liturgy.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses θρησκείᾳ τῶν ἀγγέλων as "worship the angels" without stating the genitive relation.

title: Col 3:16: "in all wisdom" with "dwell richly" or with "teaching and admonishing"?
summary: ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ can close the first clause (let the word dwell in you richly in all wisdom) or lead into the participles (in all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another).

readings.label: With "let the word dwell richly"
readings.rendering: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another
readings.grammar: ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ modifies ἐνοικείτω; the participles διδάσκοντες καὶ νουθετοῦντες begin a new phrase.

readings.label: With "teaching and admonishing"
readings.rendering: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; in all wisdom teach and admonish one another
readings.grammar: ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ modifies the participles διδάσκοντες καὶ νουθετοῦντες (the manner of mutual teaching).

macula_evidence: The tree places ἐν πάσῃ σοφίᾳ with διδάσκοντες and νουθετοῦντες as an adverbial unit, separate from ἐνοικείτω.

title: dia tou Iēsou: "asleep through Jesus" or "God will bring through Jesus"?
summary: The phrase "through Jesus" can modify the participle (those who fell asleep through/in Jesus) or the main verb ἄξει (God will bring them through Jesus, with him).

readings.label: With "those who have fallen asleep"
readings.rendering: those who have fallen asleep in Jesus, God will bring with him
readings.grammar: διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ modifies τοὺς κοιμηθέντας: death endured in Jesus (as believers).

fathers.quote: even so God will bring with him those also who sleep in Jesus.

readings.label: With "will bring"
readings.rendering: God will, through Jesus, bring with him those who have fallen asleep
readings.grammar: διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ modifies ἄξει: Jesus is the means by which God brings the dead.

macula_evidence: The tree attaches διὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ to κοιμηθέντας ("fallen asleep through Jesus").

title: "The grace of our God and Lord Jesus Christ": one person or two?
summary: One article governs "God" and "Lord" joined by καί (Granville Sharp construction), which would make Jesus Christ "our God and Lord"; but θεός is sometimes treated as a quasi-proper name, and ἡμῶν after the first noun leaves room for two persons.

readings.label: One person: Jesus is our God and Lord
readings.rendering: the grace of our God and Lord, Jesus Christ
readings.grammar: τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ: one article, two singular personal nouns of the same case, so one referent (Sharp).
readings.modern: NET, NIV footnote; Wallace argues probable

readings.label: Two persons: God (the Father) and the Lord Jesus Christ
readings.rendering: the grace of our God and of the Lord Jesus Christ
readings.grammar: The article with θεοῦ is not bound to κυρίου because θεός is treated as a quasi-proper name, or because Paul regularly distinguishes "God the Father" and "the Lord Jesus Christ".

macula_evidence: The tree parses "the grace of the God our and Lord Jesus Christ" without marking whether θεοῦ and κυρίου share a referent.

title: to katechon / ho katechōn: who or what restrains the lawless one?
summary: κατέχω can mean "restrain" or "hold sway/hold fast". The neuter τὸ κατέχον (v. 6) and the masculine ὁ κατέχων (v. 7) refer to an unnamed restrainer (neuter then person), and Paul says the readers knew.

readings.label: The Roman Empire (and its emperor)
readings.rendering: what restrains is the Roman power; he who restrains is the emperor
readings.grammar: Neuter and masculine participle = an institution and its head, transitive κατέχω = "restrain".

fathers.quote: Some indeed say, the grace of the Spirit, but others the Roman empire, to whom I most of all accede.
is arrested for a time by the continued existence of the Roman Empire.

readings.label: The Holy Spirit (or the grace of the Spirit)
readings.rendering: what restrains is the grace of the Holy Spirit
readings.grammar: Neuter τὸ κατέχον as the Spirit (πνεῦμα is neuter), masculine ὁ κατέχων as the Spirit personally.
readings.modern: Held by a minority of modern interpreters

fathers.work: Pauline Commentary from the Greek Church
fathers.quote: that which restrains is the grace of the Holy Spirit.

macula_evidence: The tree parses τὸ κατέχον and ὁ κατέχων as participles ("the one restraining") with no antecedent supplied.

title: didaskein oude authentein: two prohibitions or one?
summary: οὐδέ can join two separate prohibitions (to teach, and to exercise authority) or two elements of a single idea (to teach in a domineering manner). The meaning of αὐθεντεῖν is a related, separate lexical dispute.

readings.label: Two prohibitions
readings.rendering: I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man
readings.grammar: οὐδέ coordinates two infinitives, each negated by οὐκ ἐπιτρέπω; both are forbidden.

fathers.quote: let them not teach, but occupy the station of learners.

readings.label: One idea: teaching in a domineering way
readings.rendering: I do not permit a woman to teach in a way that usurps authority over a man
readings.grammar: οὐδέ links two terms forming a single prohibition (hendiadys); αὐθεντεῖν qualifies διδάσκειν.

macula_evidence: The tree sets διδάσκειν and οὐδὲ αὐθεντεῖν ἀνδρός as two coordinate infinitives.

title: "Saved through childbearing": which childbearing, and what salvation?
summary: διὰ τῆς τεκνογονίας has the article; it can mean "through bearing (and raising) children", "through the Childbirth" (of the Messiah), or spiritual rebirth; διά can also mean "through the pain of" (attendant circumstance).

readings.label: Through bearing and rearing children
readings.rendering: she will be saved through (the) bearing of children
readings.grammar: διά with the genitive of means or attendant circumstance; τῆς generic article; salvation as safe passage or as the woman's role.

fathers.quote: Let her not however grieve. God has given her no small consolation, that of childbearing.

readings.label: Spiritual birth of children
readings.rendering: she is saved through spiritual regeneration of children
readings.grammar: τεκνογονία interpreted figuratively: the true motherhood is spiritual rebirth.

fathers.quote: It is not having children as such that is important but this spiritual regeneration.

readings.label: Through "the Childbirth" (Christ)
readings.rendering: she will be saved through the (well-known) birth of the Child
readings.grammar: The article τῆς is definite: a unique childbearing, the Incarnation (cf. Gen 3:15, Gal 4:4).
readings.modern: Some patristic and modern interpreters; NIV note

macula_evidence: The tree glosses "saved through the childbearing" with the article but does not interpret it.

title: "The condemnation of the devil": whose?
summary: τοῦ διαβόλου can be a subjective genitive (a judgment the devil passes), or a genitive of the one condemned (the same condemnation the devil fell under).

readings.label: Judgment pronounced by the devil
readings.rendering: fall into the judgment the devil brings
readings.grammar: subjective genitive: the devil as accuser.

readings.label: The condemnation that befell the devil
readings.rendering: fall into the same condemnation as the devil
readings.grammar: objective/possessive genitive: the judgment the devil received for pride.

fathers.quote: but that he is to be condemned with the devil.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses εἰς κρίμα τοῦ διαβόλου as "condemnation the devil" without classifying the genitive.

title: "Pillar and ground of the truth": of what?
summary: στῦλος καὶ ἑδραίωμα τῆς ἀληθείας can modify "the church of the living God" or begin the confession of v. 16 (the pillar and ground of the truth, and confessedly great, is the mystery of godliness).

readings.label: The church is pillar and ground
readings.rendering: the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth
readings.grammar: The nominatives στῦλος καὶ ἑδραίωμα stand in apposition to ἐκκλησία θεοῦ ζῶντος (ἥτις).

fathers.quote: That you may know, he says, how you ought to behave yourself in the house of God, which is the Church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth. Not like that Jewish house. For it is this that maintains the faith and the preaching of the Word.

readings.label: Introducing v. 16: the mystery is pillar
readings.rendering: a pillar and ground of the truth: the mystery of godliness is great
readings.grammar: The phrase begins v. 16 as a predicate of τὸ τῆς εὐσεβείας μυστήριον.

macula_evidence: The tree places στῦλος καὶ ἑδραίωμα within the relative clause ἥτις ἐστὶν ἐκκλησία, apposed to church.

title: "Savior of all people, especially of believers": what does malista do?
summary: μάλιστα can mean "especially" (believers a subset who benefit most) or "that is, namely" (those who believe are in fact the ones saved), which affects whether the verse teaches universal provision or limits salvation to believers.

readings.label: "Especially": all are saved in some sense, believers in a fuller way
readings.rendering: the Savior of all people, especially of those who believe
readings.grammar: μάλιστα as a comparative/superlative: believers are a distinguished part of πάντων ἀνθρώπων.

fathers.quote: But if God is here the Saviour of the unbelieving, much more is He of the faithful hereafter.
The Savior of all, especially of believers, is spoken of by the apostle as one.

readings.label: "That is": the Savior of all, namely believers
readings.rendering: the Savior of all, that is, of those who believe
readings.grammar: μάλιστα = "namely" (explanatory), narrowing πάντων ἀνθρώπων to believers.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses μάλιστα as "especially".

title: "What I have entrusted": by whom?
summary: τὴν παραθήκην μου can be what I deposited with God (my life, salvation, ministry) or what was deposited with me by God (the gospel, cf. 1:14).

readings.label: What I entrusted to him
readings.rendering: he is able to guard what I have entrusted to him until that day
readings.grammar: μου is a subjective genitive: Paul is the depositor.

fathers.quote: What I have commended to him

readings.label: What was entrusted to me
readings.rendering: he is able to guard what has been entrusted to me until that day
readings.grammar: μου is an objective genitive: the deposit (the gospel) is placed with Paul.

fathers.quote: God, who committed this to us, will preserve it unimpaired. I suffer everything, that I may not be despoiled of this treasure. I am not ashamed of these things, so long as the faith is preserved uninjured.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses τὴν παραθήκην μου as "what I have entrusted".

title: "Captured by him to do his will": who are "him" and "his"?
summary: αὐτοῦ and ἐκείνου are two different pronouns: they can both refer to the devil (captured by him to do his will), or the first to the devil and the second to God (so that they return to God's will), or the first to God.

readings.label: Both the devil
readings.rendering: caught by the devil to do his will
readings.grammar: αὐτοῦ and ἐκείνου both refer to τοῦ διαβόλου; ἐκεῖνος as a distant demonstrative picking up the devil.

readings.label: "Him" the devil, "his" God
readings.rendering: caught by the devil, but (set free) to do God's will
readings.grammar: ἐκείνου distinguishes a different referent from αὐτοῦ: God, whose will they are brought back to do.

fathers.quote: Taken captive by him, he says, to His will. This no one will say relates to doctrine, but to life. For His will is that we live rightly.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses αὐτοῦ as "him" and ἐκείνου as "his" without identifying either antecedent.

title: pasa graphē theopneustos kai ōphelimos: predicate or attributive?
summary: With no verb, θεόπνευστος can be a predicate ("every Scripture is God-breathed and useful") or attributive ("every God-breathed Scripture is also useful"); and πᾶσα can mean "all" or "every".

readings.label: Predicate: all Scripture is God-breathed and profitable
readings.rendering: All Scripture is God-breathed and profitable
readings.grammar: ἐστίν is understood after γραφή; both θεόπνευστος and ὠφέλιμος are predicates.
readings.modern: KJV, RSV, NRSV, ESV, NIV, NASB

fathers.work: On the Soul and the Resurrection
fathers.quote: The Scripture is of the Holy Spirit, and its intention is the profit of men.

readings.label: Attributive: every God-breathed Scripture is also profitable
readings.rendering: Every Scripture inspired by God is also profitable
readings.grammar: θεόπνευστος is attributive; only ὠφέλιμος is predicate (καί = also).

readings.label: Restrictive: every Scripture that is profitable is inspired
readings.rendering: every Scripture suitable for edification is divinely inspired
readings.grammar: ὠφέλιμος is read with γραφή as an attributive, θεόπνευστος the predicate (Vulgate order omnis scriptura divinitus inspirata utilis).

fathers.quote: every Scripture suitable for edification is divinely inspired.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses "all scripture inspired by God and profitable" with both adjectives as predicates.

title: "Appeared to all" or "bringing salvation to all"?
summary: The dative πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις and the adjective σωτήριος can be taken together ("salvation-bringing to all") or the dative with the verb ἐπεφάνη ("appeared to all people").

readings.label: "Appeared to all people"
readings.rendering: the grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all people
readings.grammar: πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις is the dative of ἐπεφάνη; σωτήριος is attributive to χάρις.

readings.label: "Bringing salvation to all"
readings.rendering: the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all people
readings.grammar: σωτήριος with πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις: the grace brings salvation for everyone.

macula_evidence: The tree reads Ἐπεφάνη ἡ χάρις τοῦ θεοῦ σωτήριος πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις as one clause without marking the attachment of the dative.

title: "Our great God and Savior Jesus Christ": one person or two?
summary: One article governs "great God" and "Savior" (Granville Sharp), which makes Jesus Christ both; the alternative is the Father as "the great God" and Jesus as "Savior".

readings.label: One person: Jesus Christ is our great God and Savior
readings.rendering: the appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ
readings.grammar: τοῦ μεγάλου θεοῦ καὶ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ: one article, personal singular nouns, so one referent; ἐπιφάνεια is used of Christ elsewhere in the Pastorals.

fathers.quote: Where are those who say that the Son is inferior to the Father? Our great God and Saviour.
Here he calls the same both Saviour, and great God, and Jesus Christ.

readings.label: Two persons: the great God (Father) and our Savior Jesus Christ
readings.rendering: the appearing of the glory of the great God and of our Savior Jesus Christ
readings.grammar: The title μεγάλου θεοῦ is the Father's; Jesus Christ is σωτῆρος separately (KJV wording).

macula_evidence: The tree parses τοῦ μεγάλου θεοῦ καὶ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ as one noun phrase ("the great God and savior our Jesus Christ").

title: Titus 3:8: does "faithful is the saying" look back or forward?
summary: The formula "faithful is the saying" can close the previous passage (3:4-7, the gospel summary) or open the instruction that follows ("I want you to insist on these things").

readings.label: Looks back to 3:4-7
readings.rendering: The saying is trustworthy (that salvation by mercy). And concerning these I want you to insist
readings.grammar: Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος ends v. 7; καὶ περὶ τούτων begins a new sentence.

fathers.quote: These things are true, he says, and this is manifest from what has gone before.

readings.label: Looks forward
readings.rendering: This saying is trustworthy: I want you to insist on these things
readings.grammar: Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος introduces the exhortation: the "saying" is the commandment to do good works.

macula_evidence: The tree sets Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος as its own clause, with καὶ περὶ τούτων βούλομαί a separate sentence.

title: koinōnia tēs pisteōs: what is "the sharing of your faith"?
summary: The genitive can express generosity growing from faith (source), participation in the faith (objective), or the sharing/witnessing of faith (active). The prepositional phrases that follow (ἐν ἐπιγνώσει) are also variously attached.

readings.label: Generosity flowing from faith
readings.rendering: that the generous sharing that comes from your faith may become effective
readings.grammar: τῆς πίστεως is a genitive of source: κοινωνία = practical generosity, prefiguring the request about Onesimus.

fathers.quote: If you are a partaker, he says, with respect to the faith, you ought to communicate also with respect to other things.

readings.label: Participation in the faith
readings.rendering: that your fellowship in the faith may become effective
readings.grammar: τῆς πίστεως is an objective genitive: κοινωνία = shared participation in the common faith.

readings.label: Sharing (witnessing to) your faith
readings.rendering: that your evangelistic sharing of your faith may become effective
readings.grammar: κοινωνία = active sharing/imparting; the genitive is objective; ἐν ἐπιγνώσει = through understanding every good thing.

macula_evidence: The tree glosses ἡ κοινωνία τῆς πίστεώς σου as "the sharing the faith your" without classifying the genitive.
